faq.a: Vermillion is a free trivia game about finding correct answers that are less obvious. Each game has seven questions, and rarer answers earn more points.
Each accepted answer has a rarity score from 1 to 100. Less common answers can earn more points. These scores are estimates, not live survey results.

faq.q: What happens when I enter an answer the game does not know?
faq.a: An answer the game does not recognize scores nothing, and you can try again while time remains. If time runs out first, that question scores zero.
Daily Game, Endless and topic games give you 20 seconds per question. Duel gives you 15 seconds. The clock keeps going if you hide the page.
It is the same set of seven mixed questions for everyone on a UTC date. Your Daily Game score is saved once. Practice replays do not change it.
Endless gives you another seven mixed questions whenever you want. It tries to avoid questions you have seen recently when enough others are available.

One player finishes a game and shares its challenge link. The other player gets the same seven questions. If both players give the same accepted answer, both scores for that question are cut in half, rounding down.

faq.q: Can I play a topic game from an earlier date?
faq.a: Yes. Every topic has a daily game and Past games going back to November 1, 2026. Playing an older game or practicing does not replace your official topic score.
Practice lets you replay a Daily Game or topic game without using or replacing your official score. Practice games are marked separately in your browser history.

faq.q: Why did my answer not match?
faq.a: The game checks a list of accepted answers and alternate names. It can handle some small spelling mistakes, but not every name or unclear spelling. Try a standard name when you know one.
No. Scores are estimates that create a range from common to unusual answers. They do not come from personal data, accounts or player polls.

faq.q: Does the game need an account or send my scores to a server?
faq.a: No account is needed. Games, settings and scores are saved in your browser when browser storage is available. Duel links include the questions and answers needed to compare scores.
Yes. Every game mode and topic is free. There are no ads, paywalls, accounts, subscriptions or locked content.

faq.q: How do I change the display or sound?
faq.a: Use Display to choose Neon, Midnight or CRT, and Sound to turn effects on or off. Easy Read makes text larger and easier to see, and turns off scanlines and motion.
In Daily Game, Endless and Duel, each point stands for ten metres on the depth display. Topics use their own units, such as kilometres, years or energy.
Vermi is the game’s original glowing jellyfish mascot. Vermi moves and changes expression during play.
